title: Not Only Doth the Voiceful Day
description: Not Only Doth the Voiceful Day in Tonic Solfa to SAVED BY GRACE, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: William Henry Burleigh wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 89, “The Heavens Declare the Glory of God”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre Double (8.8.8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SAVED BY GRACE; any other Long Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Not on-ly doth the voice-ful day Thy lov-ing kind-ness, Lord! pro-claim, But night, with its sub-lime ar-ray Of worlds, doth mag-ni-fy Thy name. Yea, while a-dor-ing ser-a-phim Be-fore Thee bend the will-ing knee, From ev-ery star a cho-ral hymn Goes up un-ceas-ing-ly to Thee.

lines: Not only doth the voiceful day
But night, with its sublime array
Of worlds, doth magnify Thy name.
Before Thee bend the willing knee,
From every star a choral hymn
Day unto day doth utter speech,
And night to night Thy voice makes known;
Through all the earth, where thought may reach,
Is heard the glad and solemn tone;
And worlds, beyond the farthest star
Whose light hath reached a human eye,
Catch the high anthem from afar,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: William Henry Burleigh died in 1871.
credits: Words by William Henry Burleigh (1812–1871), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to SAVED BY GRACE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
